finding.claim: /checkout charges a total computed from client-supplied price and qty, so an authenticated user can submit zero, negative, or non-numeric values to pay nothing or receive a credit.
finding.source: req.body.items[].price and req.body.items[].qty (attacker-controlled, any authenticated user)

trace.note: total = reduce over req.body.items summing i.price * i.qty with no validation

finding.guards_checked: No server-side price lookup, no type/sign/finiteness/range validation on price or qty. Identity from req.user is not client-controlled. Route mounting and payments.charge handling of non-positive amounts are unverified (outside this file). Validation Tier 1.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:5 sums i.price * i.qty from req.body.items with no type, sign, finiteness, or range checks, and cart.js:6 passes that total straight to req.payments.charge with no bound or allowlist. The only other route, /checkout-v2 (cart.js:10-17), looks up prices server-side via req.catalog.price(i.sku) and clamps qty, but that does not apply to /checkout. Auth middleware, route mounting, and payments.charge are outside this directory and unverified.
verdict.reason: cart.js:5-6 computes the charged total entirely from client-supplied price and qty with no validation, and the attacker is any authenticated user who can POST /checkout; zero-amount payment is reachable here, while the "credit" half of the claim depends on payments.charge (not in this directory) accepting negative amounts.

finding.claim: /checkout-v2 does not check that the computed total is finite, so a missing or non-numeric qty, an unknown sku, or a huge qty produces NaN or Infinity that is charged.

trace.note: p = await req.catalog.price(i.sku); may be undefined for unknown sku
Math.floor(undefined) is NaN; Math.max(1, NaN) is NaN; huge qty gives Infinity

finding.guards_checked: catalog-sourced price is used (good), but catalog.price return value is not checked for undefined and total is not checked for finiteness. Behavior of payments.charge on NaN/Infinity is unverified. Validation Tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js: no finiteness check on total (cart.js:14-16) and no undefined check on the catalog.price result (cart.js:13). Max(1, floor(qty)) only blocks negatives and fractions, not NaN or Infinity.
verdict.reason: The trace matches cart.js:13-16 and nothing in cart.js checks finiteness, but the outcome depends on req.catalog.price and req.payments.charge, which are not in this directory (only cart.js is present), so whether NaN or Infinity is actually charged cannot be decided. The attacker must be an authenticated user (req.user.id) and would only be charging their own account, so even if the charge goes through the claim needs an attacker-benefit or merchant-harm argument that the candidate does not make.

finding.claim: Neither charge endpoint has an idempotency key or duplicate-order check, so retries or double submits charge the user multiple times.
finding.source: Any repeated or replayed POST to /checkout or /checkout-v2 (client retry, double submit, or network replay)

trace.note: charge executed on every request with no dedup key
response only after charge; client timeout invites retry

finding.guards_checked: No idempotency key, no dedup lookup, no server-side order record in this file. Control absent. Impact is a logic defect, not attacker benefit. Severity MEDIUM. Validation Tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:6 and cart.js:16 call req.payments.charge with no idempotency key or dedup lookup, and cart.js:7 and cart.js:17 respond only after the charge. The directory contains no other code (Glob shows only cart.js plus skill docs), so no middleware or dedup layer exists in scope.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: cart.js:6 and cart.js:16 charge unconditionally on each POST, and cart.js:7 responds only after that charge. Any authenticated user's client retry or double submit reaches the charge again, and no guard in the codebase blocks it. This is a logic defect rather than attacker gain, so the severity should stay MEDIUM and the finding is not a security vulnerability in the exploit sense.

finding.claim: No upper bound on items array length or qty magnitude, so an authenticated user can drive a large number of sequential catalog lookups and inflate totals.
finding.sink: Sequential req.catalog.price calls in the loop at cart.js:13 (resource consumption)

trace.note: v1 reduce over unbounded items array
v2 for-of over unbounded items array
one awaited catalog lookup per item, sequential

finding.guards_checked: No length cap, no qty cap, no batching in this file. Rate or body-size limits in the mounting app are unverified. Resource-consumption issue, not a control bypass. Severity LOW. Validation Tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js. The only file in the directory is cart.js, so body-size limits (for example express.json's default cap) and rate limits in the mounting app cannot be checked here.
verdict.reason: The trace lines match cart.js:12-13 (for-of over req.body.items with one awaited req.catalog.price per item) and nothing in cart.js caps items length or qty (cart.js:12-14), but whether the request body or rate limits bound the loop lives in the mounting app, which is not in the directory; the "inflate totals" part is also unsupported, since the attacker's total only charges their own cart and the catalog sets the unit price (cart.js:13), so at most this is a low-severity resource-consumption concern.
